## Overview of tutorial {.bkg-trees}

At the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

::: {.incremental}
   - Specify a survey design in R to create a survey object
   - Calculate point estimates and their standard errors with survey data 
   - Create tables and graphs incorporating survey data and standard errors
   
:::

## R Packages for Survey Analysis {.bkg-ship}

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=49%}
::: {.fragment}
- {survey} package first on CRAN in 2003
  - descriptive analysis
  - statistical testing
  - modeling
  - weighting
  
:::
::::

::: {.column width=2%}
:::

::: {.column width=49%}
::: {.fragment}
- {srvyr} package first on CRAN in 2016
  - “wrapper” for {survey} with {tidyverse}-style syntax
  - only descriptive analysis
  
:::
::::
:::::

## Why use {srvyr} over {survey}? {.bkg-ship}

::: {.incremental}

- Use the pipe function `%>%` or `|>`
- Ability to use tidy selection
- Functions follow `snake_case` convention
:::

## Brief note on pipes with {survey} {.bkg-mountains}

:::::{.columns}
::::{.column width=42%}
:::{.fragment}
Magrittr pipe (`%>%`)

:::
:::{.fragment}
- dot notation

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
design_object %>% 
  svyglm(design = ., y ~ x)
```

:::
::::

::::{.column}
:::{.fragment}
Base R pipe (`|>`)

:::

:::{.fragment}
- placeholder
    
```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
design_object |> 
  svyglm(design = _, y ~ x)
```

:::
:::{.fragment}
- anonymous (lambda) functions

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
design_object |> 
  (\(.) 
   svyglm(design = ., y ~ x)
  )()
```

:::
::::
:::::

::: aside
Check out [Isabella's article on the base pipe](https://ivelasq.rbind.io/blog/understanding-the-r-pipe/){target="_blank"}
:::

# Comparison of {dplyr} and {srvyr} Functions {background-color='{{< brand color blue >}}' .bkg-buildings}

## Apply {dplyr} functions to survey objects {.bkg-trees}

:::{.incremental}
- A few functions in {srvyr} have counterparts in {dplyr}
  - `dplyr::summarize()` and `srvyr::summarize()`
  - `dplyr::group_by()` and `srvyr::group_by()`
- Based on the object class, R will recognize which package to use

:::

## Using `summarize()` to calculate mean and median {.bkg-serpent}

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
data(api)
api_des <- apistrat |> as_survey_design(strata = stype, weights = pw)
```


::: {.panel-tabset}

### Tibble:

```{r}
#| label: summarize-tib-ex
#| code-line-numbers: "|3"
towny |> 
  summarize(
    area_mean = mean(land_area_km2, na.rm=TRUE)
  )
```

### Survey object:
```{r}
#| label: summarize-sv-ex
#| code-line-numbers: "|3"
api_des |> 
  summarize(
    score_mean = survey_mean(api99, na.rm=TRUE)
  )
```
:::


## Grouping  {.bkg-serpent}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Tibble:

```{r}
#| label: group-tib-ex
#| code-line-numbers: "|2"
towny |> 
  group_by(csd_type) |> 
  summarize(area_mean = mean(land_area_km2))
```

### Survey object:

```{r}
#| label: group-sv-ex
#| code-line-numbers: "|2"
api_des |>
  group_by(stype) |>
  summarize(score_mean = survey_mean(api99, na.rm=TRUE))
```
:::

## Using {srvyr} functions on non-survey objects {.bkg-trees}

```{r}
#| label: sv-non-svobj
#| eval: false
towny |>
  summarize(area_mean = survey_mean(land_area_km2))
```
